record.title: Study finds chat and reasoning LLMs unreliable as standalone protocol verifiers
record.summary: A September 12 journal paper evaluates GPT-5.4 and DeepSeek v4 Flash on 130 obfuscated AnB/AnBx protocols covering 388 security goals, with three runs per configuration and formal-verifier references. The authors report a chat-versus-reasoning trade-off: chat modes recall more attacks but generate many false alarms, while reasoning raises precision and misses more attacks. On their imbalanced goal set, both chat configurations score below a 77.1% always-secure accuracy baseline; agreement authentication goals remain difficult, and self-reported confidence is poorly calibrated. The paper recommends pre-screening only, with formal confirmation. These are author-reported results; the journal article and public artifact were not independently reproduced in this review.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report three runs per configuration on 130 type-aware-obfuscated AnB/AnBx protocols covering 388 security goals, comparing GPT-5.4 and DeepSeek v4 Flash chat and reasoning settings against ProVerif and OFMC verdicts.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report chat recall of 72.7% for GPT and 69.3% for DeepSeek with precision below 28%; reasoning raises reported precision to 66.5% for GPT and 45.4% for DeepSeek while recall falls to roughly 55%.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The published paper reports that the goal set contains 89 vulnerable and 299 secure goals, so a predictor that always answers secure obtains 77.1% accuracy; neither chat configuration reaches that accuracy. The authors emphasize recall rather than accuracy for this imbalanced screening task.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report persistent difficulty with injective and non-injective agreement attacks, unstable verdicts across repeated runs, and high self-reported confidence that does not reliably distinguish correct from incorrect answers. They recommend pre-screening only and formal confirmation.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: These are author-reported results, not an independent reproduction. The reviewed publisher-indexed article and repository README identify released code and experiment artifacts, but the full tables, appendices and data were not audited here.

evidence_gaps.description: The public experiment repository was identified but its commit-pinned inputs, outputs, goal labels and analysis code were not audited or independently re-scored.

The full journal article and appendices could not be opened directly because the publisher returned HTTP 429; the arXiv HTML conversion stops before the methods/results sections, so a complete version-diff was not performed.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported failure profile holds, it materially constrains the safe role of language models in protocol-security workflows: high recall comes with many false positives, while reasoning configurations still miss attacks and do not replace formal verification. This is notable evaluation evidence for a security-critical subfield, not a general bound on current LLM capability.
limitations: Results are reported by the authors and were not independently reproduced in this review.
Only GPT-5.4 and DeepSeek v4 Flash, one protocol notation, one fixed zero-shot prompt and 130 protocols are covered; transfer is unknown.
The goal set is imbalanced (89 vulnerable, 299 secure); the 77.1% always-secure accuracy baseline is not a substitute for recall or safety assessment.
The publisher page was rate-limited in this review; full methods tables, appendices, data rows, confidence intervals and exact protocol-level labels were not inspected.
Public repository availability was confirmed from its README, but no commit-pinned artifact or data audit was performed.
Reported weaknesses are specific to direct binary LLM verdicts in this experimental regime and do not establish a general capability ceiling for all models or prompt designs.
brief.summary: A September 12 journal paper evaluates GPT-5.4 and DeepSeek v4 Flash on 130 obfuscated AnB/AnBx protocols covering 388 security goals, with three runs per configuration and formal-verifier references. The authors report a chat-versus-reasoning trade-off: chat modes recall more attacks but generate many false alarms, while reasoning raises precision and misses more attacks. On their imbalanced goal set, both chat configurations score below a 77.1% always-secure accuracy baseline; agreement authentication goals remain difficult, and self-reported confidence is poorly calibrated. The paper recommends pre-screening only, with formal confirmation. These are author-reported results; the journal article and public artifact were not independently reproduced in this review.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report chat recall of 72.7% for GPT and 69.3% for DeepSeek at precision below 28%, versus higher precision but roughly 55% recall for reasoning configurations. They report poor agreement-goal detection, repeated-run instability and uninformative high self-confidence. For their imbalanced 89-vulnerable/299-secure set, the always-secure classifier obtains 77.1% accuracy and both chat configurations fall below it. The authors frame chat as possible pre-screening, not autonomous verification.
technical.demonstrated_result: The reviewed sources demonstrate that a peer-reviewed article and an author repository describing the experiment are publicly available. No experiment was independently rerun in this review.
technical.mechanism: Fixed zero-shot structured prompt over obfuscated AnB/AnBx protocol text; binary model verdicts; three runs per GPT-5.4 and DeepSeek v4 Flash chat/reasoning configuration; score against a ProVerif-first, then OFMC two-session/one-session ground-truth waterfall; disaggregate by goal type and inspect repeated-run consistency and confidence calibration.
technical.regime: Two providers, one AnB/AnBx protocol family, 130 obfuscated protocols, 388 goals, one fixed zero-shot prompt and three runs per model/mode configuration.
technical.reproducibility: The authors link code, obfuscated inputs, formal ground truth, raw outputs and comparison files in a public repository. This review inspected its README only; it did not audit version-pinned contents, re-score outputs, inspect attack traces or reproduce the analysis.
technical.strongest_baseline: Always-secure classification yields 77.1% accuracy on the study's imbalanced goal set. Formal-verifier outputs are used as reference labels. Accuracy baseline and attack-recall objective answer different questions and must not be conflated.

brief.title: Study finds chat and reasoning LLMs unreliable as standalone protocol verifiers
brief.why_it_matters: Security protocol analysis is safety-relevant and has formal verification tools with explicit semantics. The reported precision/recall trade-off and missed authentication attacks bound how these tested LLM configurations could be used: a fast language-model pass may help prioritize work, but cannot replace formal verification or justify skipping it. The result is limited to two providers, one notation family and one zero-shot prompt.
